sections.title: Headline
sections.content: DeepSeek opens its full app stack as an API, letting developers rebuild the DeepSeek App one-to-one; the day's episode is a shift in competitive focus from model benchmarks toward developer-ecosystem lock-in.

sections.title: DeepSeek opens "full-stack" application API, enabling a 1:1 rebuild of the DeepSeek App
sections.content: DeepSeek announced the opening of its full-stack application API, folding the DeepSeek App's interaction features into the existing API so that enabling the relevant parameters lets the server handle tool calls and context assembly automatically. The V4.1-Flash model (deepseek-flash) supports web search, deep-thinking search, file input, link reading and model safety across the Messages, Responses and Chat Completions interfaces. Underlying capabilities including Search, Fetch, OCR, ASR and TTS are also available as standalone interfaces, and DeepSeek open-sourced a lightweight front-end demo that can import chat history. Beyond token fees, tool calls are billed separately, with text/image search and web fetch at 5 yuan per thousand calls, OCR at 1.5 yuan per thousand pages, ASR at 0.39 yuan per hour and TTS at 1.5 yuan per ten thousand characters, with ASR and TTS at a limited-time 50% discount.
sections.significance: The most consequential event of the day: it moves competition from model benchmark scores toward developer onboarding cost and ecosystem completeness, raising the switching cost for developers who build on DeepSeek's bundled components.
sections.transition_hint: DeepSeek's move bundles application-layer tools into one API; Alibaba's Qwen is meanwhile pushing a flagship model through a restricted preview channel.

sections.title: Google DeepMind announces Gemini 4 Carbon, Gemini Decisions API and Gemini 4 Hydrogen
sections.content: Google DeepMind announced the launch of Gemini 4 Carbon, the Gemini Decisions API and Gemini 4 Hydrogen, and invited developers to share demos, builds and feedback on the new models.
sections.significance: A multi-model Gemini 4 release plus a dedicated decisions API signals Google pushing a broad model-and-API lineup into developer hands on the same day.
sections.transition_hint: Google's release is a broad model-family push; Alibaba's Qwen took a narrower, gated route for its new flagship preview.

sections.title: Alibaba Cloud releases Qwen4-Max-Preview, limited to Token Plan users until November 25
sections.content: Alibaba Cloud launched Qwen4-Max-Preview on November 11, 2026, a flagship multimodal model supporting text, image and video input with deep reasoning. It has a 1M-token context and up to 393,216 output tokens shared between thinking and final answer, with thinking enabled by default and adjustable via reasoning_effort. Access is restricted to Token Plan Personal or Team users through a dedicated base URL until November 25, 2026, with no pay-as-you-go option, and the model is expected to be taken down after the preview. It is compatible with OpenAI Chat Completions, Responses and Anthropic Messages APIs, and from this model onward max_tokens equals max_completion_tokens in Chat Completions.
sections.significance: A flagship-tier multimodal release with an unusually restrictive, time-boxed access model, testing whether gated previews can build demand before a wider launch.
sections.transition_hint: Qwen's preview is a model-access story; xAI's news is about the economics of selling an always-on agent.

sections.title: xAI ships Grok Bot 1.0 with team sharing, Slack/Teams and meeting join, as Musk concedes unit costs are unsustainable
sections.content: On November 11, xAI moved Grok Bot to 1.0, adding team-shared bots, Slack and Microsoft Teams integration, joining video meetings via link, proactive claiming of visible work, and improved browser, document and presentation reliability, at unchanged tiers of $30, $100 and $200 per month. The 1.0 release adds approval flows for team knowledge and an admin-controlled shared-login switch. Usage multiples across tiers are 4x, 15x and 50x, with weekly usage pools not shared between seats and pooled with Grok and Cursor. On November 1, Musk acknowledged on X that the cost of serving Grok Bot relative to revenue is unsustainable; SpaceX COO Gwynne Shotwell said on October 20 that Grok Bot had 800,000 paid weekly active users, more than doubling in a month.
sections.significance: A product milestone paired with an explicit admission of negative unit economics, making it the clearest test case for whether always-on agent subscriptions can be priced sustainably.
sections.transition_hint: xAI's story is about agent economics; the OpenAI item is a user backlash over a voice-mode retirement.

sections.title: OpenAI users push back on retirement of Standard and Advanced Voice in favor of GPT-Live
sections.content: In OpenAI's developer community, paying users are protesting the announced retirement of Standard Voice and Advanced Voice on December 11 in favor of GPT-Live. Complainants say GPT-Live responses are shorter and less useful for sustained complex work such as coding, document revision and research, and raise accessibility concerns, including for users with multiple sclerosis and others who cannot type for extended periods. One user reports canceling a subscription and moving to Claude and Grok; another says the altered Spruce voice also affects the regular Read Aloud function.
sections.significance: A visible user-relations and accessibility dispute over a scheduled product retirement, with reported subscription cancellations and migration to competitors.
sections.transition_hint: OpenAI's dispute concerns a consumer interface change; the Anthropic item is a third-party review of its model lineup and safety architecture.

sections.title: Review details Anthropic's November 2026 lineup and dual-envelope Fable/Mythos release
sections.content: A third-party review describes Anthropic's November 2026 lineup as Claude Fable 5.2, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, all with a 1M-token context window and effort controls, priced from $0.10 to $8 per million input tokens. It states that on November 9, 2026 Anthropic shipped Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 as the same underlying model under two safety envelopes, with Mythos restricted to organizations verified through programs such as the Cyber and Life Sciences tracks. It also describes the Responsible Scaling Policy at version 3.4 and twice-yearly redacted risk reports, most recently in February and August 2026.
sections.significance: The most detailed supplied account of Anthropic's current model tiers and its dual-envelope safety deployment, though it comes from a single third-party review rather than a primary announcement.

sections.title: Cross-Org Themes
content: Model access is being deliberately gated: Qwen4-Max-Preview is Token Plan-only until November 25, and Anthropic's Mythos is described as restricted to verified organizations.
Developer-facing API packaging is the day's competitive front, spanning DeepSeek's bundled app API, Google's Gemini Decisions API and Qwen's compatibility with OpenAI and Anthropic API formats.

sections.title: Rumors and Unverified Claims
sections.content: A third-party review claims Anthropic's November 2026 lineup is Claude Fable 5.2, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, and that Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 shipped on November 9, 2026 as one model under two safety envelopes; no primary Anthropic source was supplied. The same review's claims about Responsible Scaling Policy version 3.4 and February/August 2026 risk reports are likewise unconfirmed by supplied primary material.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: The decisive question is whether bundled application APIs and gated flagship previews actually raise developer switching costs, or merely reshuffle launch messaging. Watch for primary Anthropic confirmation of its lineup and for whether Qwen4-Max-Preview converts to general availability after its November 25 preview window.
